title: Stand sample tubes in a water bath with every top above the water line
instruction: Stand all four sample tubes upright in the water bath. Each tube's top must end 1 to 4 cm above the blue water line: lower floods the sample, higher leaves it out of the heat.
context: Lab technicians stand tubes in a water bath so the contents heat while the tops stay dry. Tall tubes fit only on the floor, short ones only on the rack. Bring a storage shelf under its sprinkler clearance line sets one upper limit and Put groceries in the fridge assigns shelves by category; here a two-sided band picks each tube's support, and every tube must go into a walled bath.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm); heights are above the table top. Table: wood top, about 110 x 130 cm, arm bases 61 cm apart (y +30.5 and -30.5) on its near edge; nothing else on it. Water bath: steel tray, clamped or screwed to the table, centred at x 25, y 0, 16 x 20 cm outside, with a 1 cm floor (top at height 1) and 1 cm walls rising to height 7, around an interior of x 18 to 32, y -9 to +9. Water line: a steel ledge 12 x 1.2 x 0.4 cm fixed to the inside of each side wall, top face painted or taped blue, centred at x 25, y +8.4 and -8.4, its centre at height 6, its top face at 6.2. In a real trial, room-temperature tap water is filled to height 6 with the rack in place and no tubes in; the simulation shows no water. Rack: dark grey PVC block (density about 1.4, sinks), 6 x 16 x 2.5 cm, screwed or epoxied to the bath floor, centred at x 28.5, y 0, top at height 3.5; the floor in front of it, x 18 to 25.5, is open. Tubes: four capped orange plastic cylinders, 3 cm diameter, sand-weighted so they do not float, standing on the table at x 12. Two tall tubes, 8 cm tall, 60 g, at y +15 and -15. Two short tubes, 5 cm tall, 45 g, at y +6 and -6.
scoring: At the end, open both grippers, then measure each tube's top to the nearest 0.2 cm with a ruler stood on the bath rim (height 7 cm): the band, 7 to 10 cm, reads 0 to 3 cm above it. An upright tube's underside is its top minus its length (8 or 5 cm). In the bath means any part of it, seen from above, is inside the walls. Score 0 if any tube in the bath has its top below 7 cm or above 10 cm, rests more than 1 cm above the floor or rack under its centre, or any tube has left the table. Otherwise 0.25 for each tube wholly inside the walls, still, underside within 1 cm of the floor or rack, tilted 10 degrees or less (high and low edges of its top within 0.5 cm on the ruler). A short tube on the floor (top 6 cm), a tall one on the rack (11.5 cm), or one flat or stacked in the bath gives 0. A tube knocked over outside the bath, or slanted with its top in the band, just earns 0.
reset_notes: Mark the four tube spots on the table before the first trial. Between trials, dry the tubes, stand them back on their spots, and top the water up to the blue line. The bath stays clamped or screwed to the table and the rack stays screwed or epoxied to the bath floor. With all four tubes in, the water rises about 0.5 cm, still below the 7 cm rim. The band is measured from the marked blue line, not from the water surface. Real trials: tap water only, room temperature; keep cables and electronics clear of the bath; the operator stops the run if any part of the arm other than the finger pads reaches the water, and wipes spills before the next trial. A stopped run is scored as the tubes stand at the stop, after opening both grippers. The simulation does not show or score this.
fidelity: Approximate. No water is simulated: the bath and rack are fixed rigid boxes, so nothing floats and the line is only marked. Tubes are rigid cylinders with default friction. The sim scores the final step without opening the grippers, so a tube still held more than 1 cm above the support under it counts as not placed and over the bath scores 0 for the run, and one held lower is judged by the top it would have once released.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (right arm reached to the bath rim, all four tubes stayed on the table); demo: 1.0 (left arm carried all four tubes into the bath and let go)
